title: Mamdani Enters Deal with N.Y.U. to Share Profits from Quantum Lab
key_facts: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a nearly $30 million city investment in a new quantum lab at NYU
The city gets 15% of revenue received by NYU's central administration from technologies developed using city-funded equipment
The lab, QFab, is expected to open in 2030 at 770 Broadway, Manhattan; about $284 million in city and university funding
NYU says it is committing $255 million; the city's share is nearly $29 million via the Economic Development Corporation
NYU projects about 2,000 permanent jobs and support for over 100 companies
Return depends on whether inventions are commercialized; Mamdani did not commit to making such deals mandatory
quote_evidence: The deal gives the city 15% of revenue received by NYU’s central administration from technologies developed using city-funded equipment at the facility, known as QFab.
Any financial return would depend on whether those technologies generate revenue.
why_it_matters_hint: Public money buys a share of future revenue instead of only a subsidy, a model the mayor says he wants to use elsewhere.
notes: NYT original blocked (403); read amNewYork's own report; NYC.gov release also listed. NYT headline is the pool item.
